In Tignes, L'Alpage des Chaudannes at the top of the Chaudannes chair, above Le Lac and Le Lavachet, serves Savoyard dishes and Savoie wines on a sun terrace. In Val Claret, La Taverne des Neiges by the Bollin and Fresse chairs looks up at the Grande Motte.
Michelin 2026: Savoie tourism. Restaurants: Snowcarbon for Val d'Isère and See Tignes for Tignes. Restaurants change hands and menus each season.

La Folie Douce on the Daille gondola above La Daille was opened by Luc Reversade in {{f:F000395}}, and once enlarged it is credited with inventing open air après clubbing. Its afternoons run to live bands, DJs and cabaret until the lifts close.

In Val d'Isère, Cocorico beside the main lift by the bus turning circle keeps the afternoon going, with La Doudoune in its basement open until five in the morning, and Dick's Tea Bar in the centre, opened in {{f:F000396}}, takes over late at night.

Tignes spreads its evenings between Le Lac and Val Claret. The Loop Bar at Le Lac can be skied to from the Trolles slope, and Strike, in the old bowling alley, claims to be the largest club in the Alps. In Val Claret, the Drop Zone has the biggest south facing terrace in Tignes by Iglu Ski's account, and the Melting Pot stays open until four in the morning.
Sources: Mon séjour en montagne on La Folie Douce (September 2023), Snowcarbon and A Luxury Travel Blog (2021) for Val d'Isère, and Iglu Ski for Tignes. Bars open and close from season to season.
How the area suits different kinds of trip, on the evidence gathered so far.
Two resorts linked by several lifts over one ridge, with no single closure that cuts them apart.
Les Brévières to Le Fornet takes {{m:all.brevieres.le-fornet|w}} lift rides each way.
Green and blue reach every sector in the map data, and the centres of the two resorts are close on easy runs.
Solaise and Le Fornet are a long way round on green and blue.
Val Claret and La Daille are one lift ride apart, so a group can split across the ridge and meet again.
The quickest ways back into Tignes Le Lac use black runs.
Free beginner lifts in Tignes, a free drag to a green run in Val d'Isère, and children under 8 ski free.
Neither resort sells a week pass of its own, so a first week pays for the whole area.
Famille Plus in both resorts, a family discount on week passes and pool entry included.
Prices for lessons and childcare vary by village and are best checked when booking.
A snowpark, a halfpipe and a boardercross in Tignes, and Val Park on Bellevarde.
Drags make up {{f:F000431}} of the main lifts on the glacier.
{{f:F000378}} black runs, the Face de Bellevarde and the highest difficult share of the Savoie areas on this site.
Off piste terrain is not controlled; the avalanche bulletin and a guide come first.
Tignes Le Lac and Val Claret start at {{f:F000420}} and {{f:F000424}}, and the season runs to {{f:F000385|dm}}.
At 1,600 m modelled snowfall has fallen, and four of the last five seasons were poor there.
The ski train reaches Bourg-Saint-Maurice, with buses on to both resorts.
The last stretch is a bus ride up the valley, and 2026/27 timetables have not yet been checked.
Day passes for Tignes or Val d'Isère alone.
There is no local week pass.
A Michelin star in each resort and mountain tables from Le Fornet to the Chaudannes.
The best known tables are expensive and book up.
The original Folie Douce, late clubs in both resorts and busy bars in Val Claret.
The two resorts are a bus ride apart in the evening.
Pools in both resorts, sledging areas in Tignes and the snow luge.
Each activity is paid for separately unless it comes with a week pass.

The catches are price and the hard way home. The six day pass is the dearest of the four Savoie areas on this site, and neither resort offers a cheaper week of its own. The fewest lift rides back into Tignes Le Lac and Les Brévières from Val d'Isère use black runs, and Le Fornet hangs on a single chair. Lower down, the modelled snow has thinned, with four of the last five seasons at 1,600 m in the lowest third.
The other large areas of Savoie

Set against its neighbours, Tignes Val d'Isère is smaller than Les 3 Vallées and Paradiski, with {{f:F000080}} of piste against {{f:F000002}} and {{f:F000071}}, but it climbs highest, to {{f:F000083}}, and has the largest share of difficult piste, {{f:F000086}}.

Its day ticket matches Paradiski's at {{f:F000067}}, but its six day pass is the dearest of the four at {{f:F000068}}. In the weather model it has the least snow of the four at 1,600 m, which matters less where Tignes Le Lac and Val Claret start at {{f:F000420}} and {{f:F000424}}.

Tignes and Val d'Isère, the two resorts on the Tignes Val d'Isère pass, split into the eight sectors that a skier meets on the ground. Sharing the pass is recorded separately from being linked by lift and piste.

A sector counts as linked only when a route of lifts and pistes reaches it in the OpenStreetMap data. Drag lifts run one way, gondolas and the two funiculars may be ridden down, and the walks from the underground Perce-Neige stations and along the Val Claret snow front are added by hand. A link is critical when closing one lift on it cuts routes that no other lift replaces. The model has not yet been checked against the official 2026/27 piste map.
Operator and measured figures are both shown and never averaged. Mapped piste from OpenStreetMap is used only to compare sectors and grades.
